Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

not only … but also conjunction

also not just … but, not merely … but also, not only … but even

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.100: nōn sōlum in praesentiā, sed etiam posterō diē
Plin. NH 9.24: nōn hominī tantum amīcum animal, vērum et mūsicae artī
Traupman 352

nōn sōlum (nōn modo, nōn tantum) … sed (vērum) etiam

adverbs and conjunctions; etiam may be left out or replaced by et

Where the first member is negative, “not only not … but even”: nōn modo … nōn …, vērum etiam; and “not only not … but not even”, nōn modo nōn … sed nē … quidem.

Other words

  • cum … tum — not only … but especially

    conjunction and adverb · also used · classical · Liv. 26.50.13: vincentem omnia cum armīs, tum benignitāte ac beneficiīs

    See both … and.

Examples

  • vestrae quidem cēnae nōn sōlum in praesentiā, sed etiam posterō diē jūcundae sunt

    your dinners are pleasant not only at the time but on the next day as wellCic. Tusc. 5.100

  • delphīnus nōn hominī tantum amīcum animal, vērum et mūsicae artī

    the dolphin, an animal friendly not only to man but also to the art of musicPlin. NH 9.24

  • senectūs nōn modo languida atque iners nōn sit, vērum etiam sit operōsa et semper agēns aliquid et mōliēns

    old age is not only not sluggish and idle, but is even busy, always doing and building somethingCic. Sen. 26

See also both … and, only, also, not even.
